Stricter evidence rules: three kinds of statement
Uneven public evidence sets each case's depth
Reading order of the cases, groups to verticals, and why Adevinta comes first
Three cross-case lessons from the comparison

results.quote: Adevinta comes first because its case is the first to ask the opening's three questions, which every later case asks again.
results.finding: Flow reader A: 'I had to re-read this. "The opening's three questions" points back to the lead paragraph ... but nothing marks those as three questions ... The reason also sounds circular: Adevinta comes first because it is the first to ask them.' The order is sound; the prose obscures the reason (the three questions are not named as such here, and the reason given is circular rather than e.g. that Adevinta is the best-documented full swing, as the spec's hand-off says).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 3, item 1 (same sentence: had to go back to find 'the opening's three questions'; reason 'nearly circular')

results.quote: the groups Adevinta, OLX and eBay Classifieds, then real estate (the fourth group, AVIV, and the property portals), then automotive
results.finding: Flow reader A: 'The opening blocks and FAILURE PATTERNS present four groups together. Here AVIV moves into the real-estate grouping, and I had to stop and reconcile the two framings. The parenthesis does explain it, so the cost was small.' The grouping is the spec's; the stumble comes from the prose naming 'the groups' as three after the callouts named four.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, section 3, item 2 (AVIV 'called one of "four groups" at the top, but here it sits under real estate ... fixes this, but only after a stumble')

results.quote: Under these rules, the cases run from whole groups to single verticals
results.finding: Flow reader B: '"Under these rules" suggests the evidence rules decide the order, but they do not. The phrase links the sections without a real connection.' Single reader.

results.quote: placed in the Chief Architect's view
results.finding: Flow reader A: 'It was briefly unclear whose Chief Architect this is: a real company's, or the book's persona? It is minor.' Single reader; a different point from reader B's (which section, not whose).

results.quote: The cases also test Veldmark, the fictional marketplace group this book follows (see [[meet-veldmark]]), and it appears only in each case's final comparison.
results.finding: Flow reader B, section 4: 'The Veldmark rule (fiction appears only in each case's final comparison, kept apart from the real record) is really an evidence rule. Moving it into "How to read the cases", or right after it, would put all the reading rules in one place.' Reader A did not suggest this (A proposed merging 'How this part connects' instead). Single reader; the point is about the declared order.

Terms the cold readers flagged as unexplained (Veldmark in the lead; Ingrid Halvorsen, Common Ground, Tradeyard, Hearthly, Motorvane, Valuo, commit tier, decision tier, tenant-separable, transitional-service terms) are all on audience.already_knows (meet-veldmark, ml-platform, multi-country-platforms, platform-consolidation). Part IX's new terms (the three kinds of statement, the Chief Architect's view, INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED, inventory or transactional bet) are glossed where first used; five-band price ratings appear as a named published fact as the spec intends. Paragraph openers start from given material.
Opens with a direct statement bridging from long-term-evolution and Veldmark to the question Part IX asks; not a placeholder, restated question, definition, 'dawn of man' or book report.
'Where to begin' synthesizes, states the reader's three-way test and hands off; no 'in conclusion' opener, no new subtopic, no body evidence.

States where the argument survives across all cases (shared layers, supply contracts, governed models) and where the record stops (product layer), which no single section states, and says what the reader can then do.
'the cases show the argument surviving ...' returns to p01's 'whether it survives contact with what real groups did'.

Cold reader names all six cases in order with the questions in the expected wording, the evidence kind (dated public records kept apart from reading and labeled inference) and the tone (measured, evidential).
Cold reader gives all three recognition rules as expected and picks case-automotive for vendor feeds and case-ebay-classifieds for a possible sale.
Cold reader says Veldmark appears only in each case's final comparison, gives both reasons, says the cases test and do not extend the scenario, and names the four 2027 choices.
